page: Amazon Web Services c8id.24xlarge is a compute-optimized instance hosted on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The platform is driven by a dedicated Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor built on the x86_64 architecture, providing 48 physical cores, 96 vCPUs at 3.9 GHz, and 480 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory configuration includes 192.0 GB of 7 GHz DDR5 RAM, establishing a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage is provided through a bundled 5,700 GB NVMe SSD array, while baseline network throughput reaches 40 Gbps.

Performance profiles exhibit top-tier throughput across multi-threaded operations. In synthetic and real-world benchmarks, the instance achieves a Geekbench multi-core score of 22,327.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 106,825.4. Native hardware extensions, including Intel AMX (tile and int8) and AVX-512, yield strong efficiency during prompt processing in large language model evaluations. Memory subsystems maintain high throughput, recording large-block read speeds of 362.34 GB/sec and small-block cached read speeds exceeding 7,650 GB/sec, complemented by a Clang compilation score of 70,004.0.

Integrating 5.7 TB of local NVMe storage reduces external block storage overhead, enhancing qualitative cost efficiency for I/O-intensive pipelines. The hardware balance favors highly parallel operations over single-thread-limited processes. With top-tier Redis performance reaching 166.59 million SET operations per second and high database benchmark scores, the instance is structured for distributed compilation, high-concurrency caching tiers, relational database engines, and compute-intensive batch processing.
description: The Amazon Web Services c8id.24xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor operating at 3.9 GHz. Utilizing the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 48 physical cores, 96 vCPUs, and 480 MB of L3 cache, backed by 192.0 GB of 7 GHz DDR5 memory and 5,700 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The server features 40 Gbps baseline networking and integrated hardware acceleration, including AVX-512 and AMX instructions. Benchmark testing indicates top-tier multi-threaded compute and data handling, highlighted by a Geekbench multi-core score of 22,327.0, a PassMark CPU score of 106,825.4, and 166.59 million Redis SET operations per second. While single-thread performance is moderate, the high core density and bundled high-capacity NVMe storage make it an effective deployment target for distributed database systems, software compilation, memory-centric caching layers, and high-concurrency batch workloads.
